role: append-only record of every plecta/params.json this repository has shipped. The anchor is the configuration the published numbers were produced under; later entries exist so a change can be made without either falsifying a dated record or silently invalidating it. tests/test_configuration_lineage.py asserts the live file is the newest entry.

lineage.note: the configuration behind every published number: heldout F1 0.8545 in benchmark_summary.json, and the 128-mask parity run in release_parity.json. Those two files record this hash and must keep recording it.
added grouping_2d.break_rings and set it to false. No pre-existing value changed. The anchor configuration always opened a matched ring; this one does not.
lineage.why: ring-breaking is a guard against a configuration the data does not produce. plecta/linking.py records it firing zero times across all 84 development scenes, so switching it off removes a step that was never taking effect. This is inert BY MEASUREMENT, not by construction: with break_rings false, break_cycles is not called at all, and any mask that did close a ring would group differently.

verified.measured_here: predict() output byte-identical with break_rings true and false on 9 masks -- the 3 real annotated crops and 6 synthetic scenes -- comparing instance count and the bytes of every layer
verified.measured_previously: 0 links dropped across all 84 development scenes, recorded in linking.break_cycles
verified.not_rerun: the 128 held-out masks, which are not present in this working tree. The published aggregates are carried over on the two measurements above, not re-measured.
verified.what_would_break_it: a mask whose matching closes a ring. None has been observed on development or held-out data, but the anchor configuration would open it and this one will not.
